title: Robo-Footballer
statementMd:
It's a beautiful April day and Wallace is playing football with his friends. But his friends do not know that Wallace actually stayed home with Gromit and sent them his robotic self instead. Robo-Wallace has several advantages over the other guys. For example, he can hit the ball directly to the specified point. And yet, the notion of a giveaway is foreign to him. The combination of these features makes the Robo-Wallace the perfect footballer — as soon as the ball gets to him, he can just aim and hit the goal. He followed this tactics in the first half of the match, but he hit the goal rarely. The opposing team has a very good goalkeeper who catches most of the balls that fly directly into the goal. But Robo-Wallace is a quick thinker, he realized that he can cheat the goalkeeper. After all, they are playing in a football box with solid walls. Robo-Wallace can kick the ball to the other side, then the goalkeeper will not try to catch the ball. Then, if the ball bounces off the wall and flies into the goal, the goal will at last be scored.

Your task is to help Robo-Wallace to detect a spot on the wall of the football box, to which the robot should kick the ball, so that the ball bounces once and only once off this wall and goes straight to the goal. In the first half of the match Robo-Wallace got a ball in the head and was severely hit. As a result, some of the schemes have been damaged. Because of the damage, Robo-Wallace can only aim to his right wall (Robo-Wallace is standing with his face to the opposing team's goal).

The football box is rectangular. Let's introduce a two-dimensional coordinate system so that point ($0$, $0$) lies in the lower left corner of the field, if you look at the box above. Robo-Wallace is playing for the team, whose goal is to the right. It is an improvised football field, so the gate of Robo-Wallace's rivals may be not in the middle of the left wall.

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/b39d273b4c5cd46a4d37ff55628a7060ed515f30.png)

In the given coordinate system you are given:

- $*y*_{1}$, $*y*_{2}$ — the $*y*$-coordinates of the side pillars of the goalposts of robo-Wallace's opponents;
- $*y*_{*w*}$ — the $*y*$-coordinate of the wall to which Robo-Wallace is aiming;
- $*x*_{*b*}$, $*y*_{*b*}$ — the coordinates of the ball's position when it is hit;
- $*r*$ — the radius of the ball.

A goal is scored when the center of the ball crosses the $*OY*$ axis in the given coordinate system between ($0$, $*y*_{1}$) and ($0$, $*y*_{2}$). The ball moves along a straight line. The ball's hit on the wall is perfectly elastic (the ball does not shrink from the hit), the angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection. If the ball bounces off the wall not to the goal, that is, if it hits the other wall or the goal post, then the opposing team catches the ball and Robo-Wallace starts looking for miscalculation and gets dysfunctional. Such an outcome, if possible, should be avoided. We assume that the ball touches an object, if the distance from the center of the ball to the object is no greater than the ball radius $*r*$.

## Input

The first and the single line contains integers $*y*_{1}$, $*y*_{2}$, $*y*_{*w*}$, $*x*_{*b*}$, $*y*_{*b*}$, $*r*$ ($1 ≤ *y*_{1}, *y*_{2}, *y*_{*w*}, *x*_{*b*}, *y*_{*b*} ≤ 10^{6}$; $*y*_{1} < *y*_{2} < *y*_{*w*}$; $*y*_{*b*} + *r* < *y*_{*w*}$; $2·*r* < *y*_{2} - *y*_{1}$).

It is guaranteed that the ball is positioned correctly in the field, doesn't cross any wall, doesn't touch the wall that Robo-Wallace is aiming at. The goal posts can't be located in the field corners.

## Output

If Robo-Wallace can't score a goal in the described manner, print "-1" (without the quotes). Otherwise, print a single number $*x*_{*w*}$ — the abscissa of his point of aiming.

If there are multiple points of aiming, print the abscissa of any of them. When checking the correctness of the answer, all comparisons are made with the permissible absolute error, equal to $10^{ - 8}$.

It is recommended to print as many characters after the decimal point as possible.

## Note

Note that in the first and third samples other correct values of abscissa $*x*_{*w*}$ are also possible.
statementZhMd:
这是一个美丽的四月天，Wallace 正在和朋友们踢足球。但他的朋友们不知道，Wallace 实际上和 Gromit 待在家里，而派出了自己的机器人替身。机器人 Wallace 比其他人有很多优势。例如，他可以把球直接踢到指定位置。然而，“送礼”这个概念对他来说却十分陌生。这些特点结合起来，使 Robo-Wallace 成为了完美的足球运动员——球一到他脚下，他就可以瞄准球门并将球踢出。上半场比赛中，他一直采用这种战术，但很少能射门得分。对方球队有一名非常出色的守门员，他能接住大多数直接飞向球门的球。

不过，Robo-Wallace 反应很快，他意识到自己可以欺骗守门员。毕竟，他们是在一个有坚固墙壁的足球场中比赛。Robo-Wallace 可以先把球踢向另一侧，这样守门员就不会尝试接球。然后，如果球从墙上反弹后飞入球门，就终于能够得分了。

你的任务是帮助 Robo-Wallace 找到足球场墙壁上的一个位置，使机器人将球踢向该位置后，球恰好从这面墙反弹一次，并沿直线飞入球门。上半场比赛中，Robo-Wallace 的头部被球击中，受了重伤。因此，一些电路损坏了。由于这次损坏，Robo-Wallace 只能瞄准自己的右侧墙壁（Robo-Wallace 面朝对方球队的球门站立）。

足球场是矩形的。我们建立一个二维坐标系：从上方俯视足球场时，点 ($0$, $0$) 位于场地的左下角。Robo-Wallace 所在球队的球门在右侧。这是一个临时搭建的足球场，因此 Robo-Wallace 对手的球门可能不在左侧墙壁的中间位置。

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/b39d273b4c5cd46a4d37ff55628a7060ed515f30.png)

在给定的坐标系中，已知：

- $*y*_{1}$、$*y*_{2}$——Robo-Wallace 对手球门两根门柱的 $*y*$ 坐标；
- $*y*_{*w*}$——Robo-Wallace 所瞄准墙壁的 $*y*$ 坐标；
- $*x*_{*b*}$、$*y*_{*b*}$——球被踢出时球的位置坐标；
- $*r*$——球的半径。

当球的中心穿过给定坐标系中的 $*OY*$ 轴，且穿过的位置位于 ($0$, $*y*_{1}$) 和 ($0$, $*y*_{2}$) 之间时，即判定进球。球沿直线运动。球与墙壁的碰撞是完全弹性的（球不会因碰撞而收缩），入射角等于反射角。如果球从墙壁反弹后无法进入球门，也就是说，如果它撞上了另一面墙或门柱，那么对方球队会接住球，而 Robo-Wallace 会开始寻找计算错误并发生故障。若这种结果有可能发生，则必须避免它。我们认为，当球心到某个物体的距离不超过球的半径 $*r*$ 时，球就接触到了该物体。

## 输入格式

第一行也是唯一一行包含整数 $*y*_{1}$、$*y*_{2}$、$*y*_{*w*}$、$*x*_{*b*}$、$*y*_{*b*}$、$*r*$（$1 ≤ *y*_{1}, *y*_{2}, *y*_{*w*}, *x*_{*b*}, *y*_{*b*} ≤ 10^{6}$；$*y*_{1} < *y*_{2} < *y*_{*w*}$；$*y*_{*b*} + *r* < *y*_{*w*}$；$2·*r* < *y*_{2} - *y*_{1}$）。

保证球在场地内放置正确，不会穿过任何墙壁，也不会接触 Robo-Wallace 所瞄准的墙壁。球门柱不会位于场地的角落。

## 输出格式

如果 Robo-Wallace 无法以所述方式进球，输出 “-1”（不含引号）。否则，输出一个数 $*x*_{*w*}$，表示他的瞄准点的横坐标。

如果存在多个瞄准点，输出其中任意一个的横坐标。判断答案正确性时，所有比较均允许绝对误差不超过 $10^{ - 8}$。

建议小数点后输出尽可能多的位数。

## 说明

注意，在第一个和第三个样例中，瞄准点横坐标 $*x*_{*w*}$ 还可以取其他正确的值。
